level1.text: A car drives round the bend of a motorway slip road at a steady speed of $20\,\text{m/s}$. The radius of the bend is $80\,\text{m}$. How large is the centripetal acceleration of the car?
A runner runs round a bend of a running track whose radius is $36.5\,\text{m}$. Her speed stays the same in the bend, $8.00\,\text{m/s}$. How large is the centripetal acceleration of the runner?

A stone of mass $0.50\,\text{kg}$ whirls on the end of a string along a horizontal circular path. The radius of the path is $1.2\,\text{m}$ and the tangential speed of the stone $4.0\,\text{m/s}$. How large is the net force on the stone?

A car drives in a roundabout whose radius is $25\,\text{m}$. An acceleration sensor shows that the centripetal acceleration of the car is $2.5\,\text{m/s}^2$. How large is the tangential speed of the car?

The radius of the drum of a washing machine is $0.25\,\text{m}$. During the spin cycle the tangential speed of a garment at the rim of the drum is $15\,\text{m/s}$. How large is the centripetal acceleration of the garment?

level2.text: A cyclist rides through the bottom of a dip in an underpass at a steady speed of $8.0\,\text{m/s}$. The combined mass of the cyclist and the bicycle is $80\,\text{kg}$, and at the bottom of the dip the radius of the arc of the road is $16\,\text{m}$. Air resistance and rolling resistance are neglected. How large is the support force of the road on the bicycle at the bottom of the dip? Give the answer in kilonewtons.

A playground roundabout turns steadily so that one revolution lasts $5.0\,\text{s}$. A child sits at the edge of the roundabout, $3.0\,\text{m}$ from the centre. How large is the centripetal acceleration of the child?

A car of mass $1200\,\text{kg}$ drives over a hill at a steady speed of $12\,\text{m/s}$. At the top of the hill the radius of the arc of the road is $30\,\text{m}$. Air resistance and rolling resistance are neglected. How large is the support force of the road on the car at the top? Give the answer in kilonewtons.

A hammer thrower whirls a hammer of mass $7.26\,\text{kg}$ before the throw. Assume that the hammer goes round a horizontal circle of radius $1.8\,\text{m}$ and one revolution lasts $0.50\,\text{s}$. How large is the net force on the hammer? Give the answer in kilonewtons.

level3.text: An icy road bends horizontally, and the radius of the bend is $60\,\text{m}$. The coefficient of static friction between the tyres and the ice is $0.10$. Air resistance and rolling resistance are neglected. What is the greatest speed at which a car can go through the bend without sliding? Give the answer in $\text{km/h}$.

A puck of mass $0.40\,\text{kg}$ is tied with a string to a peg fixed to a table, and it slides on the smooth table along a horizontal circle of radius $0.80\,\text{m}$. The string breaks if its tension exceeds $25\,\text{N}$. Friction is neglected. What is the greatest rotation frequency the puck can have?

A road designer dimensions a horizontal bend for a speed of $80\,\text{km/h}$. For safety, the friction of the road should not have to give the car a sideways force greater than $0.25$ times the weight of the car, so that the grip is enough also on a wet road. Air resistance and rolling resistance are neglected. How large must the radius of the bend be at least?
